    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source quotes a fiberwise consequence
    23	  of a state-dependent quantum linearity theorem, but suppresses two averages
    24	  and a compatibility argument for the auxiliary spaces.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One faithful theorem for a single family,
    26	  followed by a finite common-extension construction that makes the auxiliary space
    27	  uniform over the outer parameters.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite direct sums, extensions of
    29	  operators, and squared norms are standard linear algebra.  The imported
    30	  quantum linearity theorem and its state-dependent metric are project-level
    31	  inputs.
    32	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Theorem~10 of
    33	  \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, finite averaging, and extension by the identity
    34	  on orthogonal summands.  This reduction is tracked in
    35	  \ghissue{19}.
    36	\end{itemize}
    37	
    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
    41	density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
    42	indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
    43	correlation estimate
    44	\[
    45	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
    46	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
    47	\]
    48	It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
    49	binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
    50	$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
    51	\[
    52	  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
    53	  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
    54	\]
    55	Moreover,
    56	\[
    57	  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
    58	  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
    59	    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
    60	\]
    61	In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
    62	observable is invertible.
    63	
    64	The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
    65	the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
    66	the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
    67	is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
    68	formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space
    69	uniform over $(x,z)$.
    70	
    71	\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
    72	
    73	Lines~711--725 of
    74	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
    75	linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
    76	group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
    77	observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
    78	closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The quotation
    79	also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem and would
    80	unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect.  The assertion
    81	at the identity follows from exact linearity as above.
    82	
    83	Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
    84	linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
    85	single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
    86	many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
    87	to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
    88	
    89	The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
    90	with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
    91	returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
    92	one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
    93	orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
    94	observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
    95	chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
    96	or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.
    97	
    98	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
    99	
   100	The blueprint records the averaged theorem form and the common-ancilla
   101	obligation in
   102	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}, lines~82--180.  No
   103	source-labelled Lean theorem should assert pointwise closeness or a common
   104	auxiliary space until that finite-family reduction has been proved.
   105	The chapter-16 extraction statements may consume the resulting global-pair
   106	witness once the reduction is discharged; they must not assume a new
   107	fiberwise linearity hypothesis.
   108	
   109	\section{Conclusion}
   110	
   111	The primary discrepancy is a quantifier mismatch in the quotation: the cited
   112	linearity theorem gives average, not pointwise, closeness.  Its use for the
   113	family indexed by $(x,z)$ also requires an explicit finite common-extension
   114	argument.  Both are open formal reductions compatible with the intended
   115	source conclusion.

    19	\section{At a glance}
    20	
    21	\begin{itemize}
    22	  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The extraction proof contains two
    23	  incorrect numerical steps and later suppresses the range projection when
    24	  passing from unitary conjugation to isometry conjugation.
    25	  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} A corrected positive-contraction estimate,
    26	  a small-error case split for normalization, and one range-projection transfer
    27	  lemma for a projective measurement family.
    28	  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Positivity, contraction inequalities,
    29	  isometry range projections, and norm estimates belong to finite-dimensional
    30	  Hilbert-space algebra.  The state-dependent family distance and register
    31	  placements are project-local.
    32	  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The inequality
    33	  $H^2\geq2H-I$ for a positive contraction, the triangle inequality, and
    34	  $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$ for an isometry.  The repair is tracked in
    35	  \ghissue{19}.
    36	\end{itemize}
    37	
    38	\section{Key theorem forms}
    39	
    40	Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
    41	let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
    42	\[
    43	  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
    44	  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
    45	\]
    46	Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
    47	\[
    48	  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
    49	  \qquad
    50	  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
    51	\]
    52	Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
    53	\[
    54	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
    55	\]
    56	Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
    57	required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
    58	$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
    59	
    60	For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
    61	and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
    62	a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
    63	\[
    64	  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
    65	\]
    66	not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
    67	combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
    68	$\Delta$.
    69	
    70	\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
    71	
    72	Lines~1715--1742 of
    73	\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
    74	construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
    75	estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
    76	$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
    77	source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
    78	\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
    79	small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
    80	$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
    81	
    82	The triangle inequality yields
    83	\[
    84	  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
    85	\]
    86	so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
    87	$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
    88	$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
    89	universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
    90	vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
    91	are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
    92	
    93	\section{The range-projection obligation}
    94	
    95	Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
    96	obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
    97	Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
    98	those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
    99	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
   100	non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
   101	
   102	Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
   103	state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
   104	triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
   105	$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
   106	\[
   107	  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
   108	  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
   109	\]
   110	where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
   111	uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
   112	The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
   113	
   114	This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
   115	must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
   116	estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
   117	residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.
   118	
   119	\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
   120	
   121	The proof of the extraction lemma in
   122	\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex}, lines~267--274, uses the
   123	correct positive-contraction estimate and explicit small-error convention.
   124	Lines~299--330 isolate the range projection and give the transfer strategy.
   125	The chapter therefore preserves the source's state and observable conclusions
   126	while exposing the missing argument.  Stage~4.2 should provide only the
   127	concrete extraction data and comparison theorems; the range-projection lemma
   128	belongs to Stage~4.3.
   129	
   130	\section{Conclusion}
   131	
   132	The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
   133	last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
   134	argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
   135	is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
   136	the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
   137	already supplied by the extraction lemma.

   832	\subsection{Polynomials and the low-degree code}
   833	\label{sec:ld-encoding}
   834	
   835	In this section, we introduce some basic definitions about polynomials over finite fields. 
   836	An $m$-variate polynomial $f$ over $\F_q$ is a function of the form
   837	\[
   838		f(x_1,\ldots,x_m) = \sum_{\alpha \in \{0,1,\ldots,q-1\}^m} c_\alpha
   839	  x_1^{\alpha_1} \cdots x_m^{\alpha_m}
   840	\]
   841	where $\{c_\alpha\}$ is a collection of coefficients in $\F_q$.
   842	We say that $f$ has \emph{individual degree (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if
   843	$\alpha_i \leq d $ for all $1\leq i\leq m$, and that it has \emph{total degree
   844	  (at most) $d$} if $c_\alpha\neq 0$ only if $\sum_i \alpha_i \leq d$.
   845	(Affine) \emph{multilinear} polynomials are polynomials with individual degree
   846	$1$.
   847	
   848	Low-degree polynomials play an important role in this paper.
   849	For one, the classical and quantum low-degree tests of \Cref{sec:ldt} are
   850	nonlocal games that efficiently certify that the players' answers are consistent
   851	with low-degree polynomials.
   852	Low-degree polynomials are also crucial in the probabilistically checkable
   853	proofs (PCP) construction that are used in ``answer reduction'' transformation
   854	(\Cref{sec:ans}).
   855	
   856	We recall the Schwartz-Zippel lemma: 
   857	
   858	\begin{lemma}[Schwartz-Zippel lemma~\cite{Sch80,Zip79}]
   859	  \label{lem:schwartz-zippel}
   860	  Let $f, g: \F_q^m \to \F_q$ be two unequal polynomials with total degree at most $d$. Then
   861	  \begin{equation*}
   862	    \Pr_{x \sim \F_q^m}[f(x) = g(x)] \leq d/q\;.
   863	  \end{equation*}
   864	\end{lemma}
   865	
   866	
   867	\paragraph{The low-degree code.}
   868	The Schwartz-Zippel lemma implies that the set of low-degree polynomials form an
   869	error-correcting code with good distance, which we call the \emph{low-degree
   870	  code}.\footnote{It is also known as the \emph{generalized Reed-Muller code} in
   871	  the coding theory literature.}
   872	
   873	Fix an integer $m \in \N$ and let $M = 2^m$.
   874	For every $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ define the following $m$-variate multilinear
   875	polynomial over $\F_q$:
   876	\[
   877		\ind_{m,y}(x) = \prod_{i: y_i = 1} x_i \cdot \prod_{i: y_i = 0} (1 - x_i) \;.
   878	\]
   879	Here, we identify $\{0,1\}$ as a subset of $\F_q$.
   880	Notice that, when restricted to the subcube $\{0,1\}^m$, $\ind_{m, y}$ is zero
   881	everywhere except for when $x = y$.
   882	For $a\in \F_q^M$, label the coordinates of $a$ as $a_y$ for $y\in \{0,1\}^m$
   883	(identifying the latter set with $\{1,\ldots,M\}$ using, say, the lexicographic
   884	ordering on strings).
   885	For any such $a$ define the multilinear polynomial $g_a: \F_q^m \to \F_q$,
   886	called the \emph{low-degree encoding of $a$}, as follows:
   887	\begin{equation}
   888	\label{eq:ld-encoding}
   889		 g_a(x) = \sum_{y \in \{0,1\}^m} a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)\;.
   890	\end{equation}
   891	Note that for any $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, $g_a(y) = a_y$.
   892	Furthermore, the map $a\mapsto g_a$ is linear: for every $x \in \F_q^m$,
   893	\begin{equation}
   894	\label{eq:low-degree-encoding-definition}
   895		g_a(x) = a \cdot \ind_m(x)\;,
   896	\end{equation}
   897	where $\ind_m(x)$ is the vector $(\ind_{m,y}(x))_{y \in \{0,1\}^m}\in\F_q^M$.
   898	
   899	\begin{lemma}
   900	\label{lem:ld-encoding-complexity}
   901	Let $q$ be an admissible field size, and let $M = 2^m$ for some integer $m$.
   902	The complexity of computing the evaluation of the low-degree encoding $g_a(x)$,
   903	given $a \in \F_q^M$ and $x \in \F_q^m$ represented in binary, is $\poly(M,\log
   904	q)$.
   905	\end{lemma}
   906	\begin{proof}
   907		Computing $g_a(x)$ requires computing the sum of products $a_y \cdot
   908	  \ind_{m,y}(x)$ over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$.
   909	  Via \Cref{lem:efficient_arithmetic}, evaluating $\ind_{m,y}(x)$ takes time
   910	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ because it requires performing $m$ multiplications of $\F_q$
   911	  elements, and therefore the product $a_y \cdot \ind_{m,y}(x)$ requires
   912	  $\poly(m,\log q)$ time.
   913	  Computing the sum over all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$ requires $M \cdot \poly(m,\log q)
   914	  = \poly(M,\log q)$ time, as claimed.
   915	\end{proof}
   916	
   917	Finally, for any $H \subseteq \F_q$ we define the \emph{decoding} map
   918	$\coded_H(\cdot)$ which takes as input a polynomial $g : \F_q^m \to \F_q$ and
   919	returns the following vector $a \in \F_q^M$: for all $y \in \{0,1\}^m$, if $g(y)
   920	\in H$, then set $a_y = g(y)$, and otherwise set $a_y = 0$.
   921	Note that for all $a \in H^M$ we have $\coded_H(g_a) = a$ where $g_a$ is the
   922	low-degree encoding of $a$.
   923	For notational brevity we often write $\coded(\cdot)$ to denote the boolean
   924	decoding map $\coded_{\{0,1\}}(\cdot)$.

     4	/-!
     5	# Expanded registers and point measurements
     6	
     7	This module adjoins two EPR pairs to a heterogeneous Pauli-basis-test strategy,
     8	records the four register placements used in the analysis, and defines the
     9	expanded point observables and measurements.
    10	
    11	## References
    12	
    13	The constructions formalize `def:expanded-state`, `def:expanded-observables`,
    14	`def:expanded-point-measurement`, and `def:expanded-point-trace-projection` in
    15	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-874`. Their paper source is
    16	`references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-418`.
    17	-/
    18	
    19	open scoped BigOperators Matrix MatrixOrder ComplexOrder
    20	
    21	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    22	
    23	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    24	
    25	noncomputable section
    26	
    27	/-- The six registers `AA'A''BB'B''`, retaining distinct Alice and Bob local
    28	spaces. This is the register index type of `def:expanded-state`, paper
    29	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    30	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    31	abbrev SixReg (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :=
    32	  (ιA × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    33	    (ιB × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P))
    34	
    35	/-- Equality of six-register indices is supplied by classical decidability for
    36	the register type. This is the index set of `def:expanded-state`; blueprint
    37	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    38	noncomputable instance sixRegDecidableEq (P : AdmissibleParams)
    39	    (ιA ιB : Type*) : DecidableEq (SixReg P ιA ιB) :=
    40	  Classical.decEq _
    41	
    42	/-- Reassociate the tensor product of the strategy state and two EPR states
    43	directly into register order `AA'A''BB'B''` for
    44	`eq:def-psihat`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`. -/
    45	def sixRegShuffle (P : AdmissibleParams) (ιA ιB : Type*) :
    46	    (((ιA × ιB) × (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ×
    47	        (PauliRegister P × PauliRegister P)) ≃ SixReg P ιA ιB where
    48	  toFun p := ((p.1.1.1, (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    49	    (p.1.1.2, (p.2.1, p.2.2)))
    50	  invFun p := (((p.1.1, p.2.1), (p.1.2.1, p.1.2.2)),
    51	    (p.2.2.1, p.2.2.2))
    52	  left_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    53	  right_inv p := by cases p; rfl
    54	
    55	/-- The four placements `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, and `AB''` used explicitly in
    56	the chapter-14 consistency statements. Paper
    57	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
    58	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
    59	inductive Placement where
    60	  | AA'
    61	  | BA''
    62	  | BB'
    63	  | AB''
    64	  deriving DecidableEq, Repr, Inhabited, Fintype
    65	
    66	/-- The strategy-player side supplying the local Hilbert space in each of the
    67	four register placements at paper
    68	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`. -/
    69	def Placement.side : Placement → PlayerSide
    70	  | .AA' => .alice
    71	  | .BA'' => .bob
    72	  | .BB' => .bob
    73	  | .AB'' => .alice
    74	
    75	namespace ProjectiveSetting
    76	
    77	variable {P : AdmissibleParams} {ε : ℝ}
    78	
    79	/-- A strategy-local register paired with one generalized-Pauli register. This
    80	is the operator space in `def:expanded-observables`, paper
    81	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`. -/
    82	abbrev ExpandedLocalSpace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide) :=
    83	  S.LocalSpace side × PauliRegister P
    84	
    85	/-- The strategy state tensored with EPR states on `A'A''` and `B'B''`, in the
    86	six-register order. This is `eq:def-psihat`, paper
    87	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:367-372`, blueprint
    88	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:760-781`. -/
    89	noncomputable def psiHat (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) :
    90	    EuclideanSpace ℂ (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) := by
    91	  classical
    92	  exact
    93	    reindexState (sixRegShuffle P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB)
    94	      (vecTensor
    95	        (vecTensor S.toStrategy.ψ (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    96	        (eprState (PauliRegister P)))
    97	
    98	/-- Place an operator on one of `AA'`, `BA''`, `BB'`, or `AB''`, with the
    99	identity on all remaining registers. The input local space is determined by
   100	the placement, so no equality between the player spaces is assumed. Paper
   101	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:420-450`; blueprint
   102	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:876-922`. -/
   103	noncomputable def place (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (p : Placement)
   104	    (O : Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace p.side)) :
   105	    Op (SixReg P S.toStrategy.ιA S.toStrategy.ιB) :=
   106	  fun i j =>
   107	    match p with
   108	    | .AA' =>
   109	        O (i.1.1, i.1.2.1) (j.1.1, j.1.2.1) *
   110	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   111	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   112	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   113	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   114	    | .BA'' =>
   115	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   116	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   117	          O (i.2.1, i.1.2.2) (j.2.1, j.1.2.2) *
   118	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1 *
   119	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   120	    | .BB' =>
   121	        (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιA) i.1.1 j.1.1 *
   122	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   123	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   124	          O (i.2.1, i.2.2.1) (j.2.1, j.2.2.1) *
   125	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.2 j.2.2.2
   126	    | .AB'' =>
   127	        O (i.1.1, i.2.2.2) (j.1.1, j.2.2.2) *
   128	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.1 j.1.2.1 *
   129	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.1.2.2 j.1.2.2 *
   130	          (1 : Op S.toStrategy.ιB) i.2.1 j.2.1 *
   131	          (1 : Op (PauliRegister P)) i.2.2.1 j.2.2.1
   132	
   133	/-- The expanded observable
   134	`W^r(u) tensor tau^W(r * ind_m(u))` on a selected player side. This is
   135	Equation `eq:lc-23`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:374-382`,
   136	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:783-807`. -/
   137	noncomputable def expObs (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   138	    (W : PauliKind) (r : PauliScalar P) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   139	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   140	  heteroKron (S.pointObs side W r u)
   141	    (tauObservable W (fun h => r * indicatorVec u h))
   142	
   143	/-- The Fourier average defining the expanded point effect. This is the first
   144	display of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   145	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   146	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   147	noncomputable def expPointOp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   148	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   149	    Op (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   150	  averageOperatorOverDistribution (uniformDistribution (PauliScalar P)) fun r =>
   151	    phaseSign (fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)) • S.expObs side W r u
   152	
   153	/-- The Pauli-register projector onto labels whose low-degree encoding has
   154	value `a` at `u`. This is Equation `eq:qld-point-obs-def`, paper
   155	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:389-394`, blueprint
   156	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   157	noncomputable def tauPointProj (W : PauliKind)
   158	    (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) : Op (PauliRegister P) :=
   159	  ∑ h ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun h : PauliRegister P =>
   160	      dotProduct h (indicatorVec u) = a),
   161	    pauliProj W h
   162	
   163	/-- Expanded point effects are positive semidefinite. This is the positivity
   164	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   165	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   166	theorem expPointOp_nonneg (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   167	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) (a : PauliScalar P) :
   168	    0 ≤ S.expPointOp side W u a := by
   169	  sorry
   170	
   171	/-- Expanded point effects sum to the identity. This is the completeness
   172	obligation in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   173	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`. -/
   174	theorem expPointOp_sum_eq_one (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   175	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   176	    ∑ a, S.expPointOp side W u a = 1 := by
   177	  sorry
   178	
   179	/-- The complete expanded point measurement on the chosen player and Pauli
   180	register. Its effects are those of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   181	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:384-418`, blueprint
   182	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:809-844`. -/
   183	noncomputable def pointMeasExp (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε) (side : PlayerSide)
   184	    (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   185	    Measurement (PauliScalar P) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   186	  Measurement.ofSumEqOne (S.expPointOp side W u)
   187	    (S.expPointOp_nonneg side W u) (S.expPointOp_sum_eq_one side W u)
   188	
   189	/-- The expanded point effect is the convolution of the strategy point
   190	measurement and the Pauli-register point projection. This is the final display
   191	of `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   192	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   193	theorem expPointOp_eq_convolution (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   194	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   195	    (a : PauliScalar P) :
   196	    S.expPointOp side W u a =
   197	      ∑ p ∈ Finset.univ.filter (fun p : PauliScalar P × PauliScalar P =>
   198	          p.1 + p.2 = a),
   199	        heteroKron ((S.pointMeas side W u).effect p.1)
   200	          (tauPointProj W u p.2) := by
   201	  sorry
   202	
   203	/-- The expanded point measurement is projective, as asserted after the
   204	convolution formula in `def:expanded-point-measurement`, paper
   205	`14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:395-418`. -/
   206	theorem pointMeasExp_isProjective (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   207	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P) :
   208	    MIPStarRE.QPBT.Measurement.IsProjective (S.pointMeasExp side W u) := by
   209	  sorry
   210	
   211	/-- Trace-coarse-graining of the expanded point measurement. This is Equation
   212	`eq:qld-def-mptur`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`,
   213	blueprint `ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   214	noncomputable def expPointTrace (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   215	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   216	    (r : PauliScalar P) : Measurement (ZMod 2) (S.ExpandedLocalSpace side) :=
   217	  (S.pointMeasExp side W u).postprocess fun a => fixedBinTrace P.model (a * r)
   218	
   219	/-- Fourier inversion writes a trace-coarse-grained point effect as one half
   220	of the identity plus its signed expanded observable. This is Equation
   221	`eq:lc-22`, paper `14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex:411-418`, blueprint
   222	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:846-874`. -/
   223	theorem expPointTrace_eq_half_add (S : ProjectiveSetting P ε)
   224	    (side : PlayerSide) (W : PauliKind) (u : Fin P.m → PauliScalar P)
   225	    (r : PauliScalar P) (b : ZMod 2) :
   226	    (S.expPointTrace side W u r).effect b =
   227	      (2 : ℂ)⁻¹ •
   228	        (1 + phaseSign b • S.expObs side W r u) := by
   229	  sorry

   231	end ProjectiveSetting

     5	/-! # State-dependent consistency and strategy closeness
     6	
     7	The definitions are the finite-dimensional forms of `def:consistency` and
     8	`def:strategy-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-237`,
     9	from `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-288`.
    10	-/
    11	
    12	open scoped BigOperators
    13	
    14	namespace MIPStarRE.QPBT
    15	
    16	open MIPStarRE.LDT MIPStarRE.Quantum
    17	
    18	/-- The off-diagonal defect in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    19	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    20	noncomputable def consistencyDefect {X α ι : Type*}
    21	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    22	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    23	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    24	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    25	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    26	    ∑ a : α, ∑ b : α,
    27	      if a = b then 0 else
    28	        (inner ℂ ψ ((EuclideanSpace.equiv ι ℂ).symm
    29	          ((A x a * B x b).mulVec ψ))).re)
    30	
    31	/-- The quantitative relation in `def:consistency`, blueprint
    32	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:195-208`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:232-248`. -/
    33	def IsConsistentWithin {X α ι : Type*}
    34	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α]
    35	    [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    36	    (μ : Distribution X) (A B : X → α → Op ι)
    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ
    39	
    40	/-- Unit-alphabet specialization of `def:povm-distance`, blueprint
    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
    55	
    56	/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
    57	local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
    58	evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
    59	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    75	
    76	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    40	`ch14_qpbt_observables.tex:932-1032`. -/

    48	theorem deltaAnticom_isPolyErr : IsPolyErr deltaAnticom := by

    50	  intro x hx
    51	  constructor
    52	  · exact Real.sqrt_nonneg x

    77	        (fun ω (bits : ZMod 2 × ZMod 2) => S.place p
    78	          ((S.expPointTrace p.side .X ω.1 ω.2.2.1).effect bits.1 *
    79	            (S.expPointTrace p.side .Z ω.2.1 ω.2.2.2).effect bits.2))

     4	# Quantitative state and operator distances
     5	
     6	The blueprint uses asymptotic `approx` notation.  The skeleton records the
     7	corresponding squared norm functionals explicitly, leaving universal-constant
     8	estimates to later proof stages.
     9	
    10	## References
    11	
    12	These are `def:state-distance` and `def:povm-distance` in
    13	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-220`; the paper origin is
    14	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.

    24	/--
    25	Squared Euclidean distance between pure states.  Blueprint `def:state-distance`
    26	(`blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:171-179`), paper origin
    27	`references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    28	-/
    29	noncomputable def stateDistSq {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι]
    30	    [DecidableEq ι]
    31	    (ψ φ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    32	  ‖ψ - φ‖ ^ 2
    33	
    34	/--
    35	Average squared state-dependent distance between two operator families.  This
    36	is `def:povm-distance` in `blueprint/src/chapter/ch12_qpbt_games.tex:203-210`,
    37	with paper origin `references/qpbt-paper/06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:219-271`.
    38	-/
    39	noncomputable def opFamilyDistSq {X α ι : Type*}
    40	    [Fintype α] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    41	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → α → Op ι)
    42	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    43	  avgOver μ (fun x =>
    44	    ∑ a : α, ‖applyOperatorToState (M x a - N x a) ψ‖ ^ 2)
    45	
    46	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

    54	/--
    55	The phase operator `τ^Z(b)`, with the fixed binary trace in the phase.  It is

    65	  match W with
    66	  | .Z => if x = e then 1 else 0

    68	      (Real.sqrt (Fintype.card K : ℝ) : ℂ)⁻¹ * phaseSign (binTrace K (e * x))

    78	    (W : PauliKind) (e : ι → K) (x : ι → K) : ℂ :=

     4	/-!
     5	# Polynomial combination and restricted line distributions
     6	
     7	This file contains the concrete definitions at the foundation of the
     8	Chapter 15 combining argument.  A pair of bounded individual-degree
     9	polynomials is embedded into the two coordinate blocks of an extended
    10	polynomial.  On lines, explicit affine reparameterizations are composed with
    11	coefficient-list polynomials.  The original-dimensional restricted line laws
    12	are formed before decoding, while their field seed is still present.
    13	
    14	## References
    15	
    16	The combining map is `def:combine-map` in
    17	`blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex:445-480`, with paper origin

    11	\author{}

    16	
    17	\section{Purpose}
    18	
    19	This note fixes terminology for a recurring failure mode in the formalization
    20	of the low individual degree test paper, \path{arXiv:2009.12982}.  It
    21	complements the note-writing policy in \path{docs/paper-gaps/policy.tex} and
    22	the source-statement audit tracked historically in \ghissue{1458}.  The current
    23	source-boundary proof holes are tracked in \ghissue{1507} and \ghissue{422}.
    24	A proof may be blocked at
    25	an intermediate mathematical assertion.  If that assertion is added as a new
    26	hypothesis to a theorem labelled as a paper theorem, the resulting \Lean{}
    27	theorem
    28	may be correct as a conditional statement, but it is no longer the theorem in
    29	the cited source.  The apparent proof has not closed the paper theorem; it has
    30	moved a proof obligation into the theorem statement.
    31	
    32	The protocol below distinguishes such proof debt from legitimate formal
    33	boundary conditions and from genuine mathematical corrections.  It is meant for
    34	contributors and reviewers who must decide whether a bridge, residual, repair,
    35	input, or obligation structure is a proved local construction, a tracked proof
    36	gap, or statement drift which must be repaired before a theorem may be
    37	advertised as a source theorem.  The default rule is restrictive: such data
    38	must not be added to a paper-facing theorem unless it is part of the cited
    39	source statement or a documented faithful encoding of its ambient hypotheses.
    40	
    41	\section{Basic objects}
    42	
    43	\paragraph{Source theorem.}
    44	A source theorem is a theorem, lemma, proposition, or corollary in the paper
    45	source under \path{references/ldt-paper/}.  Its hypotheses and conclusion are
    46	the mathematical ground truth, subject only to faithful formal encoding and to
    47	documented paper-gap corrections.
    48	
    49	\paragraph{Paper-facing declaration.}
    50	A \Lean{} declaration is paper-facing when it is named or cited as the
    51	formalization of a source theorem, for instance through a blueprint
    52	\verb|\lean{}| link on a theorem environment carrying a paper label.  Such a
    53	declaration must match the source theorem in its public statement.  In
    54	particular, it may not add an unproved bridge, residual, repair, input,
    55	obligation structure, or other proof-obligation hypothesis which the paper does
    56	not assume.
    57	
    58	\paragraph{Proof obligation.}
    59	A proof obligation is an intermediate assertion needed by the proof of a source
    60	theorem.  It may be a construction, an estimate, a transport lemma, or a
    61	comparison between two formal representations.  If the paper proves or invokes
    62	this assertion, then the formalization should state it as a separate lemma or
    63	theorem and prove it from the upstream hypotheses.
    64	
    65	\paragraph{Obligation discharger.}
    66	An obligation discharger is a theorem or definition which constructs a proof
    67	obligation from the paper hypotheses already available at that point in the
    68	argument.  This is the preferred representation of missing work.  If the proof
    69	is not yet complete, the discharger may temporarily contain a tracked
    70	\verb|sorry|, but the paper-facing theorem should call it rather than assume
    71	its output as an additional theorem hypothesis.
    72	
    73	\paragraph{Conditional helper.}
    74	A conditional helper is a separately named theorem whose statement explicitly
    75	assumes a proof obligation.  Names such as
    76	\leanid{mainFormal\_ofInternalObligations},
    77	\leanid{orthonormalization\_ofInput}, or names whose suffix advertises the
    78	assumed obligation are permitted only when the declaration is not presented as
    79	the source theorem.  A conditional helper is a quarantine for downstream proof
    80	content; it does not close the source theorem.
    81	
    82	\section{Bridge, residual, repair, input, and obligation structures}
    83	
    84	The words \emph{bridge}, \emph{residual}, \emph{repair}, \emph{input}, and
    85	\emph{obligation structure} name possible formal shapes.  They become dangerous
    86	when their mathematical status is unclear or when their names make unproved
    87	data look like acceptable hypotheses of a source theorem.
    88	
    89	\paragraph{Bridge.}
    90	A bridge should be a transport theorem between two already defined
    91	mathematical forms: for example, a tensor-placement identity, a conversion
    92	between two equivalent consistency relations, or a statement translating a
    93	source object into a formal representation.  A bridge is harmless only after it
    94	is proved from previously available assumptions.  It becomes proof debt when it
    95	is assumed because the transport has not yet been proved.  It becomes theorem
    96	drift when the assumed bridge is added to a paper-facing theorem.
    97	
    98	\paragraph{Residual.}
    99	A residual is a named remainder after part of an argument has been performed.
   100	It is often a useful way to record the exact missing target after a completed
   101	construction.  A residual may appear as the conclusion of a helper theorem or
   102	as the input of a quarantined conditional helper.  It is not a permissible new
   103	assumption on a paper theorem unless the paper itself assumes that residual.
   104	
   105	\paragraph{Input.}
   106	An input is a named bundle of data or hypotheses consumed by a construction or
   107	conditional helper.  It is harmless only when each load-bearing field is either
   108	part of the source hypotheses or is produced by an earlier theorem.  It becomes
   109	proof debt when the bundle is merely assumed because the construction of its
   110	fields is missing.  It becomes theorem drift when such a bundle is added to the
   111	public statement of a source theorem.
   112	
   113	\paragraph{Repair.}
   114	A repair is a mathematical construction which replaces an approximate or
   115	partial object by a better object, usually with a quantitative estimate.  In
   116	the low individual degree test formalization, projectivization and
   117	orthonormalization repairs are genuine mathematical operations.  A repair
   118	should therefore appear as a construction or as a theorem discharging the
   119	corresponding obligation.  If a theorem assumes the output of the repair instead
   120	of constructing it, that theorem is conditional on the repair.
   121	
   122	\paragraph{Obligation structure.}
   123	An obligation structure is a record whose fields are the data and estimates
   124	needed by a later construction.  This is acceptable only as an internal target
   125	or as a hypothesis of a conditional helper.  Such a structure becomes statement
   126	drift if it is added to a paper-facing theorem instead of being constructed
   127	inside the proof.  The review question is whether every load-bearing field is
   128	proved from the source hypotheses or is explicitly tracked as a missing
   129	obligation.
   130	
   131	\section{The main failure mode}
   132	
   133	Suppose the paper proves
   134	\[
   135	  H \Longrightarrow C.
   136	\]
   137	During formalization, the proof may need an intermediate assertion \(B\).  The
   138	paper theorem should be represented as
   139	\[
   140	  H \Longrightarrow B \Longrightarrow C
   141	  \quad\text{inside the proof,}
   142	\]
   143	where \(B\) is obtained by a lemma or theorem from \(H\).  The following
   144	public statement is a different theorem:
   145	\[
   146	  H \land B \Longrightarrow C.
   147	\]
   148	It is not unsound in \Lean{}, but it is not the paper theorem.  It says that the
   149	conclusion follows if the missing bridge data is supplied.  Such a theorem is a
   150	conditional helper, even if its conclusion looks exactly like the paper's
   151	conclusion.
   152	
   153	This is the situation colloquially described as ``adding a bridge
   154	hypothesis''.  More precisely, an unproved intermediate step has been promoted
   155	from the proof body to the theorem's assumptions.  The correction is not to hide
   156	the hypothesis under a different structure name.  The correction is to keep a
   157	paper-facing theorem with the source statement and move the missing step to a
   158	named internal proof obligation.
   159	
   160	\section{Faithful boundary hypotheses}
   161	
   162	Not every extra formal hypothesis is a theorem drift.  Some hypotheses are
   163	faithful boundary conditions introduced by formal encoding.  Examples include
   164	nonnegativity needed for a real power, positivity needed to divide by a
   165	quantity, finiteness and nonemptiness of an index type, a field-model instance,
   166	or decidability instances required by \Lean{}.  Such hypotheses are acceptable
   167	when they express part of the mathematical ambient setting or make explicit a
   168	condition used implicitly in the paper.
   169	
   170	The distinction is load-bearing.  A faithful boundary hypothesis describes the
   171	domain in which the paper's objects live.  A proof-debt hypothesis supplies a
   172	mathematical step that the proof should derive.  If removing the hypothesis
   173	leaves an unproved construction or estimate from the paper proof, then the
   174	hypothesis is proof debt, not a boundary condition.
   175	
   176	\section{Definition drift and subtree repair}
   177	
   178	Definition drift is especially dangerous because it propagates.  If a
   179	definition is changed so that it no longer denotes the object in the paper,
   180	then every downstream theorem using that definition may continue to compile
   181	while proving statements about the wrong object.  Downstream theorem statements
   182	can then be repaired piecemeal, but the development remains unstable because
   183	the wrong definition is still upstream.
   184	
   185	When a definition mismatch is found, the repair should proceed by a subtree
   186	protocol.
   187	
   188	\begin{enumerate}
   189	  \item Identify the source object and the formal object precisely.
   190	  \item Freeze a source-faithful definition or state an adapter theorem
   191	  relating the existing definition to the source object.
   192	  \item Recheck the downstream theorem chain against that definition or adapter.
   193	  \item Re-formalize the affected subtree from the corrected interface, rather
   194	  than adding local hypotheses to each downstream theorem.
   195	  \item If a downstream proof cannot be completed, record the missing obligation
   196	  at the lowest point where the paper proof needs it.
   197	\end{enumerate}
   198	
   199	This is slower than editing a final theorem signature, but it prevents a local
   200	definition error from becoming a global theorem-statement error.
   201	
   202	\section{Allowed shapes}
   203	
   204	\begin{center}
   205	\begin{tabular}{p{0.24\linewidth}p{0.31\linewidth}p{0.32\linewidth}}
   206	\textbf{Shape} & \textbf{Allowed use} & \textbf{Forbidden use} \\
   207	\hline
   208	Paper-facing theorem & Matches the source statement up to faithful encoding &
   209	Carries non-paper bridge, residual, repair, input, obligation-structure, or
   210	proof-obligation hypotheses \\
   211	Source-shaped theorem with a tracked \verb|sorry| & Default repair when the
   212	source proof is blocked but the statement is known & Replaced by a strengthened
   213	theorem statement merely to keep the file compiling \\
   214	Conditional helper & Temporary quarantine for substantial proof content whose
   215	remaining named obligation has not yet been discharged & Introduced merely to
   216	avoid a \verb|sorry|, or linked as the source theorem or marked as
   217	proof-complete for that theorem \\
   218	Obligation discharger theorem & Constructs the obligation from paper hypotheses &
   219	Merely restates the obligation as an assumption \\
   220	Input bundle & Collects produced data for a local construction & Is assumed by a
   221	source theorem instead of being produced \\
   222	Obligation structure & Bundles constructed data and estimates & Hides unproved
   223	fields that are then assumed by a source theorem \\
   224	Paper-gap note & Documents a real mathematical or formal-statement divergence &
   225	Justifies silent statement drift without a repair plan
   226	\end{tabular}
   227	\end{center}
   228	
   229	\section{Protocol for a blocked proof}
   230	
   231	When a source-labelled proof is blocked, use the following order.
   232	
   233	\begin{enumerate}
   234	  \item Read the cited source statement and the proof passage in
   235	  \path{references/ldt-paper/}.
   236	  \item Write the paper theorem form, the current \Lean{} theorem form, and the
   237	  first missing intermediate assertion.
   238	  \item Decide whether the missing assertion is a faithful boundary condition,
   239	  a representation adapter, an ordinary lemma from the paper proof, or a real
   240	  paper-gap discrepancy.
   241	  \item If it is an ordinary lemma or adapter, create a named theorem which
   242	  discharges that obligation.  Do not add it to the source theorem as a new
   243	  hypothesis.
   244	  \item Keep the source-labelled theorem itself in the source form, even if its
   245	  proof must contain a tracked \verb|sorry|.  This is the default repair when
   246	  the missing assertion has not yet been proved.
   247	  \item Create a conditional helper only to quarantine substantial proof content
   248	  that already exists and would otherwise be lost.  Do not create such a helper
   249	  merely to avoid a \verb|sorry| or to keep making progress.  If a conditional
   250	  helper remains, give it a conditional name, keep it separate from the
   251	  paper-facing theorem, and record the obligation discharger that must eliminate
   252	  it.
   253	  \item If the source and formal statements genuinely differ, write or update a
   254	  note under \path{docs/paper-gaps/} before marking the statement as aligned.
   255	  \item Update the blueprint so that paper labels point only to paper-facing
   256	  declarations.  Conditional helpers belong in remarks or implementation
   257	  notes, not in the source theorem block.
   258	\end{enumerate}
   259	
   260	\section{Retirement criterion}
   261	
   262	An auxiliary declaration should be removed from the main blueprint route, or
   263	renamed and documented as a purely internal lemma, when all three of the
   264	following conditions hold:
   265	\begin{enumerate}
   266	  \item it is not a statement in the cited paper and is not an explicitly cited
   267	        outside result;
   268	  \item no current proof of a paper-level target needs it as stated;
   269	  \item it assumes stronger proof data, finite-length data, completion data,
   270	        repair data, synchronization data, or package fields than the paper
   271	        proof requires.
   272	\end{enumerate}
   273	If such a declaration is still useful as a formal intermediate result, it
   274	should remain a lemma or a visibly conditional helper with a planned discharge.
   275	It should not be a headline replacement for the paper theorem, and it should
   276	not support a source-labelled blueprint \verb|\leanok| claim.
   277	
   278	\section{Review questions}
   279	
   280	A reviewer should first compare every paper-labelled declaration with the cited

    37	    (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) (δ : ℝ) : Prop :=
    38	  consistencyDefect μ A B ψ ≤ δ

    41	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    42	noncomputable def opDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    43	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    44	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) : ℝ :=
    45	  opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x) (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ
    46	
    47	/-- The unit-alphabet operator distance equals its one-outcome family form from
    48	`def:povm-distance`, blueprint `ch12_qpbt_games.tex:219-226`, paper
    49	`06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:258-271`. -/
    50	theorem opDistSq_eq_opFamilyDistSq {X ι : Type*}
    51	    [Fintype X] [DecidableEq X] [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι]
    52	    (μ : Distribution X) (M N : X → Op ι) (ψ : EuclideanSpace ℂ ι) :
    53	    opDistSq μ M N ψ = opFamilyDistSq μ (fun x (_ : Unit) => M x)
    54	      (fun x (_ : Unit) => N x) ψ := rfl
    55	
    56	/-- The strategy-distance relation `def:strategy-distance`. The two strategies'
    57	local Hilbert spaces are identified, and both measurement distances are
    58	evaluated on the first strategy's state. Blueprint
    59	`ch12_qpbt_games.tex:228-237`, paper `06_nonlocal_games_and_mipstar.tex:273-285`. -/
    60	structure AreCloseStrategies (G : Game) (S S' : Strategy G) (δ : ℝ) : Prop where
    61	  /-- Identification of Alice's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    62	  hA : S.ιA = S'.ιA
    63	  /-- Identification of Bob's local Hilbert spaces. -/
    64	  hB : S.ιB = S'.ιB
    65	  state : stateDistSq S.ψ (reindexState
    66	      (Equiv.prodCongr (Equiv.cast hA).symm (Equiv.cast hB).symm) S'.ψ) ≤ δ
    67	  alice : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.fst)
    68	      (fun x a => heteroKron ((S.A x).effect a) 1)
    69	      (fun x a => heteroKron (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hA) ((S'.A x).effect a)) 1)
    70	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    71	  bob : opFamilyDistSq (G.μ.map Prod.snd)
    72	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 ((S.B y).effect b))
    73	      (fun y b => heteroKron 1 (reindexOp (Equiv.cast hB) ((S'.B y).effect b)))
    74	      S.ψ ≤ δ
    75	
    76	end MIPStarRE.QPBT

  1669	\begin{lemma}
  1670	\label{lem:qld-unitary}
  1671	There exists a function $\delta_\qld(\eps,m,d,q) = O(\delta_S^{1/4} + md/q)$ (where $\delta_S$ is defined in \Cref{lem:qld-4-7}) and unitaries $V_\alice$ acting on registers $\alice \alice' \alice''$ and $V_\bob$ acting on $\bob \bob' \bob''$ such that 
  1672	\begin{enumerate}
  1673		\item There exists a state $\ket{\aux}$ on registers $\alice \alice' \bob \bob'$ such that
  1674		\[
  1675			\left \| V_\alice \otimes V_\bob \ket{\hat{\psi}}_{\alice \alice' \alice'' \bob \bob' \bob''} - \ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''} \right \|^2 \leq \delta_\qld.
  1676		\]
  1677		
  1678		\item For all $W \in \{X,Z\}, h \in \F_q^\nqubits$
  1679		\begin{align*}
  1680			V_\alice \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h \Big)_{\alice} \, V_\alice^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\alice \alice'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\alice''} \\
  1681			 V_\bob \, \Big(M^{(\Pauli,W)}_h  \Big)_{\bob}\, V_\bob^\dagger &\approx_{\delta_\qld} \Id_{\bob \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_h)_{\bob''}
  1682		\end{align*}
  1683		where the $\approx$ statements hold with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice \alice' \bob \bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes \nqubits}_{\alice'' \bob''}$.

  1692	\]

     3	In this appendix we give a proof of \Cref{thm:pauli}. For
     4	convenience, we repeat the statement of the theorem here.
     5	
     6	\begin{theorem}
     7	  \label{thm:pauli-appendix}
     8	There exists a function 
     9	\[\delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q) = a(md)^a(\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd})\]
    10	 for universal constants $a \geq 1$ and $0 < b < 1$ such that the following holds. For all admissible parameter tuples $\qldparams = (q,m,d)$ and for all strategies $\strategy = (\ket{\psi},A,B)$ for the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ that succeed with probability at least $1 - \eps$, there exist local isometries $\phi_\alice: \mH_\alice \to \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\alice''},\phi_\bob: \mH_\bob \to \mH_{\bob'} \otimes \mH_{\bob''}$ (where $\ket{\psi} \in \mH_\alice \otimes \mH_\bob$ and $\mH_{\alice''},\mH_{\bob''} \cong (\C^q)^{\otimes M}$ with $M = 2^m$) and a state $\ket{\aux} \in \mH_{\alice'} \otimes \mH_{\bob'}$ such that 
    11	\begin{enumerate}
    12	    \item $\left \| \phi_\alice \otimes \phi_B \ket{\psi} - \ket{\aux} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}  \right \| \leq \delta_{\qld}(\eps,m,d,q)$,
    13	    \item Letting $\tilde{A}^x_a = \phi_A\, A^x_a \, \phi_A^\dagger$ and $\tilde{B}^y_b = \phi_B B^y_b \phi_B^\dagger$, we have for $W \in \{X,Z\}$
    14	    \begin{gather*}
    15	        \tilde{A}^{(\pauli,W)}_u \otimes I_{\bob'\bob''} \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} (\tau^W_u)_{\alice''} \otimes I_{\alice' \bob' \bob''} \\
    16	        I_{\alice'\alice''} \otimes \tilde{B}^{(\pauli,W)}_u    \approx_{\delta_{\qld}} I_{\alice' \alice'' \bob'} \otimes (\tau^W_u)_{\bob''}\;,
    17	    \end{gather*}
    18	    where the $\approx_{\delta_{\qld}}$ statement holds with respect to the state $\ket{\aux}_{\alice'\bob'} \otimes \ket{\EPR_q}^{\otimes M}_{\alice''\bob''}$ and the answer summation is over $u \in \F_q^M$.
    19	\end{enumerate}
    20	\end{theorem}
    21	We also recall the meaning of the parameters: $q$ is the field size,
    22	$m$ the number of variables, $d$ the degree of the low-degree code,
    23	and $\nqubits=2^m$ is the number of $\ket{\EPR_q}$ states being tested for.
    24	
    25	This appendix is structured as follows. First, we establish some preliminary facts and definitions 
    26	in \Cref{sec:qld-prelim}. In the remainder of the appendix, we
    27	show \Cref{thm:pauli-appendix} by showing how to construct a representation of
    28	the Pauli group on the provers' Hilbert space, starting from a
    29	strategy $\strategy$ that succeeds in $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ with
    30	high probability. This is done in several stages: in
    31	\Cref{sec:commutation}, we use the strategy measurements to define a
    32	set of observables that correspond to a subset of the Pauli $X$ and
    33	$Z$ observables, and show that these
    34	approximately satisfy the associated Pauli group relations. In \Cref{sec:expanding},
    35	we adjoin ancillary registers containing EPR states to the provers'
    36	state $\ket{\psi}$, and define a new set of approximately-commuting
    37	observables acting on the expanded state. In \Cref{sec:combining}, we
    38	combine the approximately-commuting observables into a strategy for
    39	the \emph{classical} low-degree test, and in \Cref{sec:apply-ldt}, we
    40	apply the soundness theorem of the classical low-degree test to
    41	construct a single projective measurement that simultaneously measures all of the
    42	approximately-commuting observables. Finally, in
    43	\Cref{sec:separating}, we use this single simultaneous measurement to
    44	construct an exact representation of the Pauli group, show that it
    45	is close to the original strategy observables on the expanded state, and deduce that the game $\game^\pauli_\qldparams$ is a self-test for the strategy $\strategy^\pauli$.

new file mode 100644
index 0000000..78bf9bd
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/paper-gaps/qpbt_cross-basis-phase.tex
@@ -0,0 +1,109 @@
+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
+
+\input{command}
+\renewcommand{\ghissue}[1]{%
+  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/#1}{GitHub issue \##1}}
+
+\title{The Cross-Basis Phase in the Extracted Pauli Observables}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-03}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Low.  The source drops a nontrivial phase when the
+  two binary-basis indices are distinct.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One exact multiplication calculation for
+  generalized Pauli observables; no robustness estimate changes.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite-sum bilinearity and the field
+  trace are standard algebra.  The extracted-observable product form and the
+  project's phase convention are project-local.
+  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The generalized Pauli commutation
+  relation and nondegeneracy of the trace pairing.  The local correction is
+  tracked in \ghissue{19}.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+Let $e_1,\ldots,e_t$ be the fixed self-dual basis of $\mathbb F_q$ over
+$\mathbb F_2$.  With the phase convention of the source, generalized Pauli
+observables satisfy
+\[
+  \tau^X(a)\tau^Z(b)
+  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(a\mathbin{\cdot}b)}
+   \tau^Z(b)\tau^X(a).
+\]
+Substituting $a=e_j\widetilde u$ and $b=e_{j'}\widetilde v$ gives the exact
+relation
+\[
+  \widetilde X^j(\widetilde u)\widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)
+  =(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}
+      (e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v))}
+   \widetilde Z^{j'}(\widetilde v)\widetilde X^j(\widetilde u).
+\]
+This formula applies uniformly, whether or not $j=j'$.
+
+\section{The false dichotomy in the source}
+
+Lines~1438--1450 of
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
+identify each extracted observable with a tensor product containing
+$\tau^W(e_j\widetilde u)$.  Lines~1451--1456 then claim that the extracted
+$X$- and $Z$-observables commute whenever $j\neq j'$
+\cite[lines~1438--1456]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  Self-duality gives only
+\[
+  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'})=0 \qquad (j\neq j').
+\]
+It does not imply
+\[
+  \operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}s)=0
+  \qquad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb F_q.
+\]
+
+Indeed, for distinct $j,j'$, the element $c=e_je_{j'}$ is nonzero.  The trace
+pairing is nondegenerate, so there is an $s\in\mathbb F_q$ for which
+$\operatorname{tr}(cs)=1$.  Taking vectors whose first coordinates are $1$
+and $s$, with all remaining coordinates zero, gives
+$\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v=s$.  The two extracted observables
+then anticommute.  This is a counterexample to the printed cross-basis
+commutation assertion.
+
+When $\widetilde u\mathbin{\cdot}\widetilde v$ lies in the prime field, the
+printed distinction is recovered from self-duality.  The chapter quantifies
+over arbitrary vectors, however, so that special case does not repair its
+statement.
+
+\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
+
+The discussion following the product-form calculation in
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex}, lines~69--95, records
+the full phase and notes that the false dichotomy is not used later in the
+extraction argument.  A formal theorem may therefore retain the mathematically
+correct uniform phase relation with a \textbf{Local fix} marker.  It must not
+assert exact commutation merely from $j\neq j'$.
+
+This correction changes neither the definition of the extracted observables
+nor the source-faithful consistency and extraction conclusions.  It repairs an
+auxiliary algebraic assertion that is independent of the robustness estimates.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The source's cross-basis commutation claim is false for general
+$\widetilde u$ and $\widetilde v$.  The correct relation retains the phase
+$(-1)^{\operatorname{tr}(e_je_{j'}(\widetilde u\cdot\widetilde v))}$.
+Because the later argument does not invoke the false dichotomy, this is a
+local correction rather than an additional hypothesis on the extraction
+theorem.
+
+\bibliographystyle{alpha}
+\bibliography{references}
+
+\end{document}

+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
+
+\input{command}
+\renewcommand{\ghissue}[1]{%
+  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/#1}{GitHub issue \##1}}
+
+\title{The Decoding Identity in the Pauli Extraction Argument}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-03}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source applies a decoder--encoder
+  identity to every bounded individual-degree polynomial, although the identity
+  is guaranteed for encoded polynomials and can fail outside the encoding image.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One restricted algebraic identity and one
+  probabilistic estimate showing that the constructed measurement assigns
+  little state-dependent mass to outcomes outside the encoding image.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Evaluation of the multilinear
+  interpolant is elementary polynomial algebra.  The non-encoding-mass bound
+  uses project-specific consistency estimates and Schwartz--Zippel.
+  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Multilinear interpolation on the
+  Boolean cube, injectivity of the low-degree encoding, measurement
+  consistency, and Schwartz--Zippel.  The correction is tracked in
+  \ghissue{19}.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+For a word $h\colon\{0,1\}^m\to\mathbb F_q$, let $g_h$ be its multilinear
+extension.  Define the chapter's decoder by
+\[
+  \operatorname{Dec}(g)(y)=g(y),
+  \qquad y\in\{0,1\}^m.
+\]
+Then
+\[
+  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h
+  \quad\text{and}\quad
+  \operatorname{Dec}(g_h)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g_h(u).
+\]
+More generally, the second identity holds for a polynomial outcome $g$ under
+the explicit hypothesis that $g$ belongs to the image of the encoding; no
+converse is asserted.
+
+For an arbitrary bounded individual-degree polynomial $g$, the Boolean values
+determine its multilinear interpolant, not necessarily $g$ itself.  The
+unrestricted identity
+\[
+  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_m(u)=g(u)
+\]
+is therefore false.
+
+\section{Counterexample and source comparison}
+
+The low-degree encoding is defined at lines~873--897 of
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/04_preliminaries.tex}.  The general decoder at
+lines~917--924 retains evaluations lying in a chosen subset $H$; the extraction
+chapter instead specifies at lines~1419--1420 of
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} that the
+decoder returns all evaluations on the Boolean cube.  This is the specialization
+$H=\mathbb F_q$, rather than the Boolean-valued shorthand used earlier
+\cite[lines~873--924 and 1419--1420]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
+
+Take $m=1$, $d\geq2$, and a field of characteristic two with more than two
+elements.  For $g(x)=x^2$, the Boolean evaluations are $g(0)=0$ and $g(1)=1$.
+Consequently the decoder is the word whose multilinear extension is $x$.
+For any $u\notin\{0,1\}$ with $u^2\neq u$,
+\[
+  \operatorname{Dec}(g)\mathbin{\cdot}\operatorname{ind}_1(u)=u
+  \neq u^2=g(u).
+\]
+Thus the equality asserted for every $g$ at lines~1483--1492 of the chapter-14
+source mirror is false \cite[lines~1483--1492]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  If degrees at
+least $q$ are allowed, equality as a function would not by itself prove encoding
+membership either, since $x^q$ and $x$ induce the same function on $\mathbb F_q$.
+
+\section{Required repair}
+
+The extraction proof must split the marginal measurement into encoding and
+non-encoding outcomes.  On encoding outcomes, the restricted identity above
+justifies the substitution.  On the complement, the proof must bound
+\[
+  \sum_{g\ \mathrm{not\ an\ encoding}}
+  \langle\widehat\psi,\widehat S_g^W\widehat\psi\rangle.
+\]
+The blueprint derives an $O(\delta_S)+md/q$ bound from point consistency and
+the combined point measurement.  A non-encoding polynomial differs from every
+encoded polynomial, so Schwartz--Zippel bounds the probability that their
+evaluations coincide.  This estimate is the open reduction; it must be proved
+from the paper hypotheses rather than inserted as an extraction hypothesis.
+
+The conjugation calculation at lines~1805--1822 does not require the false
+unrestricted identity.  Its decoder term cancels against the outcome shift,
+and only linearity of $h\mapsto g_h$ and the genuine identity
+$\operatorname{Dec}(g_h)=h$ are needed
+\cite[lines~1805--1822]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
+
+\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
+
+The decoding-identity remark and the proof of the pulled-apart consistency
+lemma in
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex} state the restricted
+identity and isolate the non-encoding-mass estimate.  The Lean API should
+therefore require encoding membership at every use of the dot-product
+evaluation theorem.  No unrestricted theorem, residual assumption, or witness
+field is source-faithful.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The decoding identity is false for a general polynomial outcome.  Restricting
+it to the encoding image is a necessary local correction.  Recovering the
+source's measurement-consistency conclusion then requires the separate
+non-encoding-mass estimate, which remains an open proof obligation.
+
+\bibliographystyle{alpha}
+\bibliography{references}
+
+\end{document}

+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}
+\setlength{\emergencystretch}{2em}
+
+\input{command}
+\renewcommand{\ghissue}[1]{%
+  \href{https://github.com/Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A/issues/#1}{GitHub issue \##1}}
+
+\title{Triangle Estimates and Isometry Transfer in Pauli Extraction}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-03}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The extraction proof contains two
+  incorrect numerical steps and later suppresses the range projection when
+  passing from unitary conjugation to isometry conjugation.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} A corrected positive-contraction estimate,
+  a small-error case split for normalization, and one range-projection transfer
+  lemma for a projective measurement family.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Positivity, contraction inequalities,
+  isometry range projections, and norm estimates belong to finite-dimensional
+  Hilbert-space algebra.  The state-dependent family distance and register
+  placements are project-local.
+  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} The inequality
+  $H^2\geq2H-I$ for a positive contraction, the triangle inequality, and
+  $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$ for an isometry.  The repair is tracked in
+  \ghissue{19}.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+Let $H_X$ and $H_Z$ be the positive contractions of the extraction proof, and
+let $\vartheta$ be a unit vector such that
+\[
+  \langle\vartheta,H_W\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta/2
+  \qquad (W\in\{X,Z\}).
+\]
+Since $(I-H_W)^2\geq0$,
+\[
+  H_W^2\geq2H_W-I,
+  \qquad
+  \langle\vartheta,H_W^2\vartheta\rangle\geq1-\delta.
+\]
+Also $\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert^2\leq\delta$, whence
+\[
+  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert^2\leq4\delta.
+\]
+Together with $H_XH_Z$ equal to the EPR projection, these estimates give the
+required overlap bound, with constants absorbed into the stated
+$O(\sqrt\delta)$ error.
+
+For the final transfer, let $\phi\colon\mathcal H\to\mathcal K$ be an isometry
+and set $Q=\phi\phi^\dagger$.  If $N_h$ is the unitary-conjugated extension of
+a measurement operator $M_h$, then the exact identity is
+\[
+  \phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ=QN_h,
+\]
+not merely $N_h$.  Thus comparison of $N_h$ with an ideal projector must be
+combined with control of $(I-Q)\Delta$ on the ideal comparison state
+$\Delta$.
+
+\section{Numerical defects in the source proof}
+
+Lines~1715--1742 of
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex}
+construct $H_X,H_Z$ and identify $H_XH_Z$ with the EPR projection.  The norm
+estimate at lines~1743--1750 gives
+$\lVert(I-H_W)\vartheta\rVert\leq\sqrt\delta$.  At lines~1753--1757 the
+source substitutes $\delta$ inside the reverse triangle inequality
+\cite[lines~1715--1783]{Ji2020MIPStar}.  That replacement is not valid for
+small $\delta$.  The desired lower bound on
+$\langle H_W^2\rangle$ follows directly from $H_W^2\geq2H_W-I$, as above.
+
+The triangle inequality yields
+\[
+  \lVert H_X\vartheta-H_Z\vartheta\rVert\leq2\sqrt\delta,
+\]
+so its square is at most $4\delta$.  Line~1761 instead bounds that square by
+$2\sqrt\delta$ without a stated restriction.  This inequality follows when
+$\delta\leq1/4$; for larger error the theorem is made trivial by enlarging the
+universal constant.  The same small-error split ensures that the projected
+vector defined at lines~1769--1773 is nonzero before it is normalized.  These
+are local numerical repairs and do not weaken the extraction conclusion.
+
+\section{The range-projection obligation}
+
+Lines~1827--1858 prove state-dependent closeness for the concrete operators
+obtained by conjugating the original measurement with the swap unitaries.
+Lines~1864--1875 then define isometries by adjoining EPR pairs and applying
+those unitaries, and immediately state the corresponding closeness for
+$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger$.  The omitted range projection makes this implication
+non-definitional \cite[lines~1827--1875]{Ji2020MIPStar}.
+
+Let $\Psi$ be the original state and suppose $\phi\Psi$ is close to the ideal
+state $\Delta$.  Since $Q\phi\Psi=\phi\Psi$ and $Q$ is a contraction, the
+triangle inequality bounds $(I-Q)\Delta$ by the state-extraction error.  Using
+$\phi M_h\phi^\dagger=N_hQ$, split
+\[
+  (N_hQ-T_h)\Delta
+  =(N_h-T_h)\Delta-N_h(I-Q)\Delta,
+\]
+where $T_h$ is the ideal Pauli projector.  Summing squared norms over $h$
+uses projectivity and orthogonality to keep the second term under control.
+The same argument is required for each player and each Pauli basis.
+
+This transfer is an open proof obligation for the next extraction stage.  It
+must be a theorem derived from the concrete swap unitaries, transformed-state
+estimate, and operator comparisons.  It must not be stored as a bridge field,
+residual assumption, or hypothesis of the source-labelled soundness theorem.
+
+\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
+
+The proof of the extraction lemma in
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch16_qpbt_extraction.tex}, lines~267--274, uses the
+correct positive-contraction estimate and explicit small-error convention.
+Lines~299--330 isolate the range projection and give the transfer strategy.
+The chapter therefore preserves the source's state and observable conclusions
+while exposing the missing argument.  Stage~4.2 should provide only the
+concrete extraction data and comparison theorems; the range-projection lemma
+belongs to Stage~4.3.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The printed triangle calculation has repairable numerical errors, and the
+last passage from unitaries to isometries omits a genuine range-projection
+argument.  Neither defect is a counterexample to Pauli soundness.  The former
+is corrected by positive-contraction inequalities and a small-error split;
+the latter remains a named downstream proof obligation whose hypotheses are
+already supplied by the extraction lemma.
+

+\documentclass[11pt]{article}
+
+\usepackage{amsmath,amssymb}
+\usepackage{xurl}
+\usepackage[hidelinks]{hyperref}

+\title{The Quoted Quantum Linearity Theorem in the Pauli Basis Analysis}
+\author{}
+\date{2026-09-03}
+
+\begin{document}
+\maketitle
+
+\section{At a glance}
+
+\begin{itemize}
+  \item \textbf{Difficulty.} Medium.  The source quotes a fiberwise consequence
+  of a state-dependent quantum linearity theorem, but suppresses two averages
+  and a compatibility argument for the auxiliary spaces.
+  \item \textbf{Estimated weight.} One faithful theorem for a single family,
+  followed by a finite common-extension construction that makes the auxiliary space
+  uniform over the outer parameters.
+  \item \textbf{Mathlib/project split.} Finite direct sums, extensions of
+  operators, and squared norms are standard linear algebra.  The imported
+  quantum linearity theorem and its state-dependent metric are project-level
+  inputs.
+  \item \textbf{Key mathematical inputs.} Theorem~10 of
+  \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}, finite averaging, and extension by the identity
+  on orthogonal summands.  This reduction is tracked in
+  \ghissue{19}.
+\end{itemize}
+
+\section{Key theorem forms}
+
+Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hilbert space, let $\rho$ be an arbitrary
+density operator on $H$, and let $u\mapsto O^u$ be binary observables on $H$,
+indexed by $\mathbb F_2^t$.  The cited theorem assumes the averaged
+correlation estimate
+\[
+  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u,v}
+  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left(O^u O^v O^{u+v}\rho\right) \geq 1-\delta.
+\]
+It produces an auxiliary space $H'$, a unit vector $\mathrm{anc}\in H'$, and
+binary observables $L^u$ on $H\otimes H'$ satisfying, with
+$\rho'=\rho\otimes|\mathrm{anc}\rangle\langle\mathrm{anc}|$,
+\[
+  L^uL^v=L^{u+v}
+  \quad\text{for every }u,v.
+\]
+Moreover,
+\[
+  \mathop{\mathbb E}_{u}
+  \operatorname{Tr}\!\left((L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})^\dagger
+    (L^u-O^u\otimes I_{H'})\,\rho'\right)\leq\delta.
+\]
+In particular, $L^0=I$: exact linearity gives $(L^0)^2=L^0$, while an
+observable is invertible.
+
+The chapter needs a parameterized version.  For each pair $(x,z)$ it applies
+the theorem to $(r,s)\mapsto O^{x,z,r,s}$.  Since the provider theorem accepts
+the actual nonnegative defect on each fiber, no assumption that a fiber defect
+is at most one, and no good--bad fiber split, is needed.  One must still
+formulate the finite common-extension step that makes the auxiliary space
+uniform over $(x,z)$.
+
+\section{Comparison with the quoted statement}
+
+Lines~711--725 of
+\path{references/qpbt-paper/14_analysis_of_the_pauli_basis_test.tex} quote the
+linearity theorem.  The displayed hypothesis correctly averages over both
+group variables.  The displayed conclusion, however, says that the corrected
+observable is close for every $u$, whereas Theorem~10 of the cited work gives
+closeness only on average over $u$ \cite{Natarajan2017Linearity}.  The quotation
+also inserts $\delta\leq1$, which is absent from the provider theorem and would
+unnecessarily obstruct applying it with a fiber's actual defect.  The assertion
+at the identity follows from exact linearity as above.
+
+Lines~825--832 construct the family $O^{x,z,r,s}$ and establish approximate
+linearity only after averaging over $x,z,r,r',s,s'$.  They then apply the
+single-family theorem separately for every $(x,z)$ and state that sufficiently
+many zero ancillas avoid a further extension.  The remaining implicit step is
+to make the theorem's possibly fiber-dependent auxiliary spaces uniform.
+
+The finite setting admits a standard repair.  Apply the theorem on each fiber
+with its actual defect, choose one finite auxiliary space large enough for all
+returned spaces, and embed each returned space so that its unit vector maps to
+one fixed vector.  Extend the conjugated observables by the identity on the
+orthogonal complement.  The embeddings may depend on the fiber because the
+observables do.  Averaging then yields the conclusion used later in the
+chapter.  This is an open reduction, not a counterexample to the quoted theorem
+or to the source's eventual combined-measurement conclusion.
+
+\section{Blueprint and formalization status}
+
+The blueprint records the averaged theorem form and the common-ancilla
+obligation in
+\path{blueprint/src/chapter/ch15_qpbt_combining.tex}, lines~82--180.  No
+source-labelled Lean theorem should assert pointwise closeness or a common
+auxiliary space until that finite-family reduction has been proved.
+The chapter-16 extraction statements may consume the resulting global-pair
+witness once the reduction is discharged; they must not assume a new
+fiberwise linearity hypothesis.
+
+\section{Conclusion}
+
+The primary discrepancy is a quantifier mismatch in the quotation: the cited
+linearity theorem gives average, not pointwise, closeness.  Its use for the
+family indexed by $(x,z)$ also requires an explicit finite common-extension
+argument.  Both are open formal reductions compatible with the intended
+source conclusion.
+
+\bibliographystyle{alpha}
+\bibliography{references}
+
+\end{document}
